Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection, while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth.﴾

Tafsir of Surah al-Mumtahanah

It is Madani, and Allah knows best.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾. The verse was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah when he wrote a letter to the polytheists informing them of some of the affair of the Prophet. The report about this is what al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hasan al-Shafi'i, the Abu Ali, informed us: Abu al-Hasan ibn Faras informed us: Abu Muhammad al-Muqri' informed us: my grandfather Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' informed us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', who said: I heard Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, say: "The Messenger of Allah sent me, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and said: 'Set out to Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman riding a camel with her a letter.' So we set out, our horses galloping with us, until we reached Rawdat Khakh, and there we found the woman riding a camel, and we said to her: 'Bring out the letter.' She said: 'I have no letter with me.' We said: 'You will surely bring out the letter, or we will strip you of your clothes.' So she brought out a letter from the braid of her hair. We took it and brought it to the Prophet, and behold, it was a letter from Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah to the polytheists in Makkah, informing them of some of the affair of the Prophet. The Prophet summoned Hatib and said to him: 'What is this?' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, do not hasten against me. I was a man attached to Quraysh, meaning an ally, and I was not of their own kin, and those of the Muhajirun who are with you have their relatives, relatives through whom they protect their kin, and I had no relative in Makkah, so I wished, since that had escaped me, to make a hand with them by which they would protect my relatives. By Allah, I did not do it out of doubt in Islam, nor out of contentment with disbelief.' The Prophet said: 'He has spoken the truth to you.' Umar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, let me strike the neck of this hypocrite.' The Prophet said: 'He has witnessed Badr, and perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you.'"

The people of tafsir said: "When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, intended a raid, he would conceal it by means of others, and he used to say: 'War is deception.' So when he intended to march on Makkah, he concealed his affair with the utmost concealment, and Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, through a woman named Sarah, wrote a letter to the people of Makkah informing them of the Prophet's march. Allah informed His Prophet of that, and the matter was as we have explained, and Allah, Exalted, revealed this verse."

His saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. In the verse there is evidence that Hatib did not leave faith by that act.

His saying: ﴿do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾, that is, My enemies and your enemies, and they are the polytheists of Quraysh.

His saying: ﴿showing them affection﴾, that is, you convey to them the news of the Prophet and his secret through the affection that is between you and them. It is also said: ﴿showing them affection﴾ means "with counsel," as said by Muqatil. It was also said: ﴿showing them affection﴾ means "by the letter." That is called affection, and likewise counsel, because that is evidence of affection.

His saying: ﴿while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth﴾. The waw is the waw of circumstance, as said by al-Zajjaj. Its meaning: and their state is that they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth.

His saying: ﴿They expel the Messenger and you﴾, that is, they expelled the Messenger and expelled you. The meaning of expulsion here is compulsion to depart.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿because you believe in Allah, your Lord﴾, that is, because you believed in Allah, your Lord.

His saying: ﴿if you have gone out to strive in My way﴾. They said: in the verse there is inversion and reordering, and the meaning is: if you have gone out to strive in My way and seeking My pleasure, then do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies. It was also said its meaning is: do not secretly show them affection if you have gone out to strive in My way and seeking My pleasure; this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿you show them affection secretly﴾, a report in the sense of a prohibition.

His saying: ﴿And I know best what you conceal and what you declare﴾, that is, what you keep secret and what you make apparent.

His saying: ﴿And whoever of you does that has strayed from the right way﴾, that is, has erred from the path of truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 2:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If they overcome you, they will be enemies to you﴾. Its meaning: if they gain control over you (ẓafar, yaẓfarū bikum). The Arabs say: "So-and-so is thaqif laqif," when he is quick to seize (thaqif, "skilled at overtaking," laqif, "quick at seizing").

And His saying: ﴿they will be enemies to you﴾, i.e., they will deal with you in the manner of enemies.

And His saying: ﴿and will stretch out to you their hands and their tongues with evil﴾, i.e., their hands with the sword, and their tongues with abuse.

And His saying: ﴿They wish that you would disbelieve﴾, i.e., they love that you would disbelieve just as they disbelieved.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Your relatives and your children will never benefit you﴾. It means: you did what you did for the sake of your kinship ties and your relatives, and that will never benefit you on the Day of Resurrection.

And His saying: ﴿On the Day of Resurrection He will distinguish between you﴾. That is: He will distinguish between you on the Day of Resurrection; so the people of obedience will be sent to Paradise, and the people of disobedience to the Fire.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 4:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed there has been for you an excellent pattern in the Messenger of Allah﴾, meaning: an excellent exemplar (qudwah hasanah).

And His saying: ﴿in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship other than Allah. We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever"﴾. The meaning in all of this is that He commanded them to emulate Abraham in disavowing the polytheists and abandoning allegiance with them.

And His saying: ﴿except for the saying of Abraham to his father, "I will surely seek forgiveness for you, but I have no power to do anything for you against Allah"﴾. Qatadah said: its meaning is, "Emulate Abraham except in this matter," which is his seeking forgiveness for his polytheist father. We have already explained the reason for Abraham's seeking forgiveness for his father earlier. And His saying: ﴿and I have no power to do anything for you against Allah﴾, meaning: I cannot ward off from you anything from Allah. This is the saying of Abraham to his father.

And His saying: ﴿Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned in repentance, and to You is the final return﴾ is a report about Abraham and his believing people, meaning: they said that.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve﴾. Mujahid and others said: that is, do not punish us at the hands of the disbelievers, nor with a punishment from You, lest the disbelievers think that we are upon other than the truth because You punished us, and so it becomes a trial for them in their religion, and they think that we were upon falsehood. For they would say: "If these people were upon the truth, they would not have been punished, nor would they have been defeated."

And His saying: ﴿And forgive us, our Lord; indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 6:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed there has been for you an excellent example in them﴾. He repeated the first meaning by way of emphasis.

And His saying: ﴿for whoever hopes for Allah and the Last Day﴾, i.e., fears Allah and fears the Day of Resurrection.

And His saying: ﴿But whoever turns away - indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾, i.e., the One who is independent of them, the Praiseworthy in His actions. The meaning is: when they oppose His command and take the disbelievers as allies, nothing of that returns to Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Perhaps Allah﴾ — we have already explained that "perhaps" (ʿasā) from Allah is obligatory (wājib).

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿will bring about affection between you and those among them with whom you have enmity﴾ — most of the exegetes hold that what is meant by this is the marriage of Umm Habība, daughter of Abū Sufyān, to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It has also been said that it refers to the conversion to Islam of Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb, Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith, Suhayl ibn ʿAmr, Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām, Ṣafwān ibn Umayya, and others. In some tafsirs it is related that when the Prophet died, Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb was the governor (amīr) over some of Yemen; when the Arabs apostatized, he fought Hawdhah al-Ḥimār and his people over their apostasy, and so he was the first to strive (jihād) alongside those who had apostatized.

And His saying: ﴿and Allah is Powerful﴾ — that is, He is able to bring about affection between you and them.

And His saying: ﴿and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ — that is, for what came from them before their Islam and before the affection arose between you and them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 8:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion and do not expel you from your homes﴾. Concerning this there are several opinions. The first: that what is meant are people among the disbelievers in the time of the Prophet from Khuza'ah, and they are Mudlij and others. The third opinion: that Qutaylah [was an unbeliever, and] was the mother of Asma'. Asma' did not accept her gift until she asked the Prophet (ﷺ), so Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse and permitted accepting and reciprocating it. This was related by Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr.

The fourth opinion: that this was before the revelation of the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf), and it was abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword. Qatadah and others said this.

As for His saying: ﴿that you show them kindness and deal with them justly﴾, that is: that you do good to them and practise justice (qist, 'adl) toward them, that is, reciprocate.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾, that is: those who do justice.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah only forbids you from those who fight you over religion, expel you from your homes, and back up [others] in your expulsion﴾. That is: they helped one another in expelling you.

And His saying: ﴿that you take them as allies﴾. Its meaning: that you take them as allies (tatawallawhum).

And His saying: ﴿And whoever takes them as allies, then those are the wrongdoers﴾. That is: they placed loyalty (al-muwalah) in other than its proper place.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants﴾ He called them believers before their arrival at the Prophet because they were intending faith, and this is their designation. This was mentioned by al-Azhari.

And His saying: ﴿then test them﴾ meaning: examine them. The people of tafsir said: the verse was revealed concerning the agreement that existed between the Prophet and the polytheists, which was the Treaty of Hudaybiyah. The Prophet had agreed with the polytheists that whoever came to him from among them he would return to them, and whoever joined them from among the believers they would not return. Then God, exalted is He, abrogated this agreement, lifted it concerning women, and commanded examination. He said: ﴿If you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers; they are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them. And give them what they have spent. And there is no blame upon you in marrying them when you have given them their bridal payments. And do not hold onto marriage bonds with disbelieving women﴾. Some of them said: the agreement was unrestricted, and there was no explicit provision regarding returning the women to them. Others said: there was an explicit provision that the women were to be returned to them even if they came as believers, and then it was abrogated; and this is the more well-known view. So the woman who came as a believing emigrant after the agreement was Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt. As for the examination (imtihan), Ibn Abbas said: it is that she is made to swear that she did not emigrate except out of love for God and His Messenger, and desire for Islam, and that she did not emigrate because of an incident she had caused, nor out of hatred for a husband, nor out of desire for wealth, nor out of love for a person.

And His saying: ﴿God knows best their faith﴾ means: their sincerity in their faith.

And His saying: ﴿If you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers﴾. If someone says: How is one to reconcile His saying ﴿If you know them to be believers﴾ with His saying ﴿God knows best their faith﴾? The answer: the meaning of ﴿If you know them to be believers﴾ is the faith of profession and examination, as if they had professed faith and sworn at the examination.

And His saying: ﴿do not return them to the disbelievers﴾ means: do not send them back.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿they are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them﴾ means: they are not lawful for the disbelievers in marriage, nor are the disbelievers lawful for the believing women in marriage.

And His saying: ﴿and give them what they have spent﴾: God obligated the Muslims to return to their husbands what the husbands had given them as dowries.

And His saying: ﴿and there is no blame upon you in marrying them when you have given them their bridal payments﴾ means: their dowries. And in this is evidence that marriage is not valid except with a dowry.

And His saying: ﴿and do not hold onto marriage bonds with disbelieving women﴾ means: do not keep marriage with disbelieving women. The meaning is that when a man embraces Islam and emigrates to us, leaving his wife behind in the abode of war as a disbeliever, her status is disregarded and there remains no marriage between him and her. It is narrated that when Umar, may God be pleased with him, emigrated, he left behind two polytheist wives in Mecca; then one of them was married to Mu'awiyah, and the other to Safwan ibn Umayyah.

And His saying: ﴿and ask for what you have spent﴾ means: what you have given. This concerns a Muslim woman who joined the polytheists, when her husband demanded from the polytheists the dowry he had given her.

And His saying: ﴿and let them ask for what they have spent﴾ means: what they gave as dowry, which is what we mentioned earlier. This is not a command, and it is not obligatory that they necessarily ask; rather its meaning is: if they ask, they are to be given. All of this is abrogated, and it had been a covenant between the Messenger and them, and that has been lifted.

And His saying: ﴿That is the judgment of God; He judges between you, and God is Knowing and Wise﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if any of your wives escape you to the disbelievers﴾, meaning: one of your wives has gone over to the disbelievers, namely the women. ﴿And you then gain (fa'aqabtum)﴾, meaning: you take booty. Al-Qutaybi said: its meaning is that you had a turn of good fortune in the spoils and in victory. It was also read as "fa'qabtum" (you gained in turn), and it carries that same meaning.

His saying: ﴿Then give to those whose wives have gone the like of what they spent﴾, meaning: the like of what they had given as the bridal gift (mahr). The meaning of the verse is: when a Muslim's wife joins the polytheists and they do not return the bridal gift, and the Muslims gain victory over them and take booty, they shall return to the husband from the booty taken the bridal gift that he had given.

His saying: ﴿And fear God, in whom you are believers﴾, meaning: in whom you have faith. This ruling is also abrogated (mansukh).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 12:

God Most High says: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with God, will not steal, will not commit adultery, will not kill their children⦆, the verse. It was revealed concerning the pledge of allegiance of women. He had pledged the men only to faith and jihad, but he pledged the women to all these things. It is related that the Prophet sat on al-Safa when Makkah was conquered, and ʿUmar sat below him, and the women came to pledge allegiance to him, and among them was Hind bint ʿUtbah, veiled and disguised. When the Prophet said, "We pledge to you that you will not associate anything with God," Hind said, "We did not come to you while there remains in our hearts any polytheism." When he said, "And that you will not steal," Hind said, "I have taken from the property of Abu Sufyan such-and-such and such-and-such, and I do not know whether you will make it lawful for me or not?" Abu Sufyan was present, and he said, "I make it lawful for you for what has passed and for what remains." In another narration: when she said that, the Prophet recognised her and said, "Are you Hind bint [ʿUtbah]?" She said, "Yes. Pardon what has passed, O Prophet of God; may God pardon you." He said, "Indeed Islam wipes out what came before it." When the Prophet said, "And that you will not commit adultery," Hind said, "Does a free woman commit adultery?!" ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, laughed. When he said, "And that you will not kill your children," meaning: do not bury your daughters alive, Hind said, "We raised them young, and you killed them grown." Her son Handhalah ibn Abi Sufyan had been killed on the day of Badr. When [he] said, ﴿nor bring a slander that they have forged between their hands and their feet⦆, Hind said, "I know slander only as ugly." 

The meaning of the verse: the woman should not attribute to her husband a child that is not his, ﴿nor bring a slander that they have forged between their hands and their feet, nor disobey you in what is right, then pledge allegiance to them⦆. It was also said that its meaning is: that she picks up a child and says to her husband, "This is my child by you." Whoever holds this view says: this is preferable, because God Most High said, ﴿nor commit adultery⦆, so the prohibition on adultery is already contained in the first meaning, and therefore this must have another meaning.

As for His words, ﴿they have forged between their hands and their feet⦆: He said this because when a child falls from a woman it falls between her hands and feet. It was also said: because the breast is between the hands, and the private part is between the legs, and the woman gives birth and nurses. It was also said: the mention of the hands and feet is for emphasis, like His words, ﴿that is for what your hands have [sent forth]⦆, meaning: for what you have earned, and the mention of the hands is for emphasis.

When the Prophet said, "And do not disobey me in what is right," Hind said, "We did not come to you to disobey you." It is related that she said, "Indeed you command noble morals."

As for "what is right" (al-maʿruf), there are two opinions: one is that it encompasses all acts of obedience; the other is that it is wailing (al-niyahah) and what women do over the dead, such as tearing garments, scratching faces, cutting hair, and the like. This second view is the more well known, and Umm ʿAtiyyah related it traced back to the Prophet, explaining it as wailing. In some narrations: "No woman fulfilled that except Umm ʿAtiyyah." Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi related in his Jami', through the narration of Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah al-Ansariyyah, that a woman among the women said, "What is this 'what is right' in which we must not disobey you?" He said, "Do not wail." She said, "O Messenger of God, the Banu so-and-so have supported me in mourning my uncle, and it is necessary to repay them, so I reproached him repeatedly, and he permitted me to repay them. Then I did not wail after that, neither for repaying them nor for anything else, until now. And no woman remained except that she wailed, other than me." The Shaykh al-Imam said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Qaffal informed us of that, Abu al-ʿAbbas ibn Siraj informed us, Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Mahbubi informed us, Abu ʿIsa informed us, ʿAbd ibn Humayd informed us, from Abu Nuʿaym, from Yazid ibn ʿAbd [Allah] al-Shaybani, from Shahr ibn Hawshab... the hadith. Abu ʿIsa said: Umm Salamah al-Ansariyyah is Asma bint Yazid al-Sakuniyyah.

As for His words, ﴿so pledge allegiance to them and ask God's forgiveness for them⦆, meaning: God has forgiven them.

As for His words, ﴿indeed God is Forgiving, Merciful⦆, we have already explained it. It is established through the narration of ʿAisha that the Prophet never touched the hand of a woman except a woman he owned. The well-known account of the pledge of the women is that he called for a vessel containing water, dipped his hand in it, and every woman who pledged dipped her hand in it. It has also been said that he took their hands behind a garment, but the first is more correct.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah is angry﴾. In this there is a return to the story of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, and an emphasis on the prohibition of allying with the disbelievers. It was also said: the verse is general in its application.

His saying: ﴿a people with whom Allah is angry﴾. It was said: they are the hypocrites. It was also said: they are the Jews. According to the first opinion, they are the polytheists.

His saying: ﴿who have despaired of the Hereafter﴾, meaning: they have despaired of resurrection after death. This is clear regarding the polytheists, for they used to deny resurrection, and Allah, may He be exalted, has informed of them that they said: ﴿It is not but our worldly life; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time﴾. Likewise, it is clear regarding the hypocrites. But if we take it to refer to the Jews, then the meaning of the verse is the Jews who used to know the Prophet, knowing that he was a Prophet of Allah, yet denied his prophethood out of envy and rebellion. The meaning of their despair of the Hereafter is despair of reward, for when they recognised the truth [and denied it], being obstinate, they came to know with certainty that they would be in the Fire in the Hereafter. It was also said: according to this opinion, the meaning is that the Jews used to say: there is no eating, no drinking, and no enjoyment in Paradise; so the meaning of despair is their despair of these blessings, because of their belief.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿as the disbelievers have despaired of the companions of the graves﴾. In this there are two opinions. The first: as the disbelievers have despaired of the companions of the graves of attaining reward and reaching Paradise, for they witnessed the matter and knew with certainty that they were people of the Fire.

The second opinion: as the disbelievers have despaired of the companions of the graves, that they will not return to them. According to the first opinion, the disbelievers meant are those who have died; according to the second opinion, the disbelievers meant are the living among them. And Allah knows best.
